narrative.overview:
Artificer Toolkit is a product UI first. It is not trying to look like a marketing site dressed up as an app, and it is not trying to romanticize complexity. The system is built around one idea: serious tabletop authoring work should feel ordered, legible, and dependable, even when the underlying data model is dense. The interface should feel like a well-laid-out workbench, not a toy chest and not an enterprise relic.

The visual language is restrained, but not cold. A cyan-led accent system gives the product a recognizable identity without turning every screen into a branded poster. Neutral surfaces do most of the work. Color is used to orient, confirm, and prioritize. The system rejects cluttered form pages, decorative gradients as a default move, and dense authoring screens that reveal everything at once.

This system explicitly rejects the anti-references captured in PRODUCT.md: Azure DevOps form clutter, D&D Beyond content-creation brittleness, and any UI that treats responsive support as secondary. Desktop and mobile are equal citizens.
keyCharacteristics: Dense when needed, but always navigable
Dual-theme by design, not as an afterthought

rules.name: The Accent Scarcity Rule
rules.body: Cyan is a directional signal, not wallpaper. Most screens should read as neutral first, with cyan used to show focus, action, or state.

rules.name: The Dual-Surface Rule
rules.body: Light and dark themes keep the same hierarchy. Do not redesign the interface per theme. Invert the surfaces, preserve the structure.

rules.name: The Density Hierarchy Rule
rules.body: Dense screens do not use hero type. Large type is reserved for true entry moments, not repeated work surfaces.

rules.name: The One-Step Rule
rules.body: Move between adjacent sizes with purpose. Flat scales make the product feel vague and cluttered.

rules.name: The Flat-at-Rest Rule
rules.body: Resting content stays quiet. Elevation appears when a surface genuinely needs separation or interaction state.

dos: Do keep authored screens neutral-first, with cyan reserved for action, focus, and state.
Do preserve the same information hierarchy across light and dark themes.
Do use framed surfaces only when they clarify structure or interaction.
Do make desktop and mobile layouts feel intentionally composed, not mechanically collapsed.
Do keep long-form authoring surfaces strongly sectioned, with obvious location and next-action cues.
donts: Don't recreate Azure DevOps forms: avoid cluttered pages, weak hierarchy, and outdated organization patterns for dense authoring flows.
Don't recreate D&D Beyond content creation: avoid brittle creation flows, weak data structure, and poor conditional disclosure.
Don't treat responsive support as secondary: desktop and mobile both need intentional layouts rather than desktop-first leftovers.
Don't use decorative gradients, glassmorphism, or side-stripe card accents as default styling moves.
Don't turn every repeated surface into an identical card grid. Density needs hierarchy, not repetition.
